messages:
alex: FYI — cutover for feature flag `enable-response-cache` is scheduled for 08:00 UTC in the change window. Plan:
- 08:00: canary (5%)
- +15m: 25%
- +30m: 100%
Rollback conditions: error rate > 0.5% or p95 latency increase > 300ms. Link to notes: https://redwood.internal/notes/FF-847

maya: sounds good. who will watch metrics during the ramp? i can cover first 30m then sanjay takes over. :thumbsup:

alex: perfect — i'll kick off the toggle and monitor traces. i'll post canary logs to the thread.

deploy-bot: [08:00:05] action: `ff.rollout.start` flag="enable-response-cache" target=canary-1 rollout=5% actor=alex

alex: kicked it at 08:00:05. running the rollout command so it's auditable:
```
/ff toggle enable-response-cache --env prod --group canary-1 --percent 5 --by alex
```

maya: metrics look clean at +2m. error rate 0.03%, p95 = 240ms. no obvious request errors. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: noticed a small spike on worker-3 health checks at +4m but looks unrelated to cache key eviction. checking logs.

alex: if worker-3 is noisy we hold the 25% step, don't proceed until we confirm.

deploy-bot: [08:15:12] action: `ff.rollout.update` flag="enable-response-cache" target=canary-1 rollout=25% actor=alex

emily: heads-up — had one customer report a malformed response (trace id 0af3c). i've pulled the span, looks like a serialization edge-case. sending to @sanjay

sanjay: got it, looking at trace 0af3c now. initial hunch: deserialization with newer cache proto when payload size > 8kb.

maya: should we pause at 25% and run a quick compatibility check across 10k requests? i can trigger a load-run in staging with prod payload samples.

alex: agree. pausing ramp. do not go to 100%.

deploy-bot: [08:22:40] action: `ff.rollout.pause` flag="enable-response-cache" target=canary-1 actor=alex reason="investigating serialization"

maya: started the staged compatibility test now, using sampled payloads. expected runtime ~8m.

emily: i posted the malformed payload sample in the #eng-runtime thread and added a diff of the cache proto change.

sanjay: located the failing code path. easy fix — guard against empty metadata and fallback to legacy serializer. will open a tiny patch; ETA 12m.

alex: thanks. plan: apply hotfix, run canary compatibility job, then resume rollout to 100% if all green. if another malformed response appears post-fix, we rollback the feature flag to 0% immediately and open a postmortem.

deploy-bot: [08:41:05] action: `deploy.patch.applied` patch="ff-serialize-fallback" actor=sanjay env=prod

maya: compatibility run finished, 0 failures in 10k sampled requests. p95 stable at 248ms.

alex: resuming to 100% now. command:
```
/ff toggle enable-response-cache --env prod --group canary-1 --percent 100 --by alex --note "hotfix applied; compatibility verified"
```

deploy-bot: [08:49:30] action: `ff.rollout.update` flag="enable-response-cache" target=canary-1 rollout=100% actor=alex

maya: monitoring — all clear so far. no recurrence of malformed responses in the last 10m.

sanjay: leaving a small follow-up PR to add telemetry coverage for serialization failures.

alex: closing out: update release notes with the incident and mitigation steps, mark rollout as successful. great cross-team response. :tada:
